newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-JONES WINS PHOENIX OPEN BY 11 STROKES, JUST MISSES RECORD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-JONES WINS PHOENIX OPEN BY 11 STROKES, JUST MISSES RECORD.

text.p: Steve Jones birdied the last two holes to win the Phoenix Open by 11 shots Sunday, but fell one stroke short of equalling the all-time PGA Tour scoring record.

Jones shot a final-round 67 to finish at 26 under par, 11 in front of Sweden's Jesper Parnevik, who also had a 67. Nick Price of Zimbabwe was alone in third place at 14 under after a three-under-par 69.

"Thank God it's over," said Jones of his wire-to-wire victory, the sixth win of his career and the first since he won the U.S. Open last June. "This is the kind of result you can never predict. My goal after winning the U.S. Open was to prove I could win again."
The 11-stroke margin of victory is the greatest on tour since Jose Maria Olazabal won the World Series of Golf by 12 in 1990.

Jones thought the tour scoring record, set by Ben Hogan in 1945 and matched by Mike Souchak in 1955, was 26 under par rather than 27, and so he believed he had made it. "I'm on the last hole, I've got the tournament won, and yet I'm feeling pressure. When does the pressure stop?"

For the rest of the field the pressure stopped when Jones began his round by sinking two 25-foot putts, on the first hole for birdie and the next hole for par. "My putter was phenomenal. I ought to have it bronzed when I'm done," said Jones.

Parnevik, who won the tournament for second place when he edged past Price, recorded his best finish on the U.S. tour ever, his previous best having come last week at the Bob Hope Classic when he shot a final-round 62 to finish third.

Because Parnevik plays full-time in America and is no longer a European tour member, he cannot earn Ryder Cup points. He hopes that playing well in the United States will lead Seve Ballesteros to name him as one of the two captain's selections for the September matches.

Jones, on the other hand, moved into the top 10 on the U.S. Ryder Cup point list with his third top-10 finish this year. Jones also moved into first place on the 1997 money list, his $270,000 earnings in Phoenix giving him a $346,414 total.
